gaps.sentence: If only I ___ more at university!
gaps.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' — regret about a past failure.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ his temper in the meeting yesterday.
gaps.hint: past regret with wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect: had not lost.

gaps.sentence: If I had known you were coming, I ___ a cake.
gaps.hint: unreal past result, would have participle
gaps.explanation: The result of an unreal past condition is 'would have' plus the past participle: would have baked.

gaps.sentence: She'd be a great lawyer if she ___ more patient.
gaps.explanation: Second conditional with 'be': 'were' for all persons.

gaps.sentence: He would be healthier if he ___ so much red meat.
gaps.hint: an unreal present habit, past simple
gaps.explanation: For an unreal present habit, the if-clause uses the past simple: did not eat.

gaps.sentence: If he had not left his passport at home, he ___ the earlier flight.
gaps.hint: third conditional result, would have participle
gaps.explanation: The unreal past result takes 'would have' plus the participle: would have caught.

gaps.sentence: Had I ___ the risks, I would never have invested.
gaps.explanation: After inverted 'Had I', the past participle follows: known.

gaps.sentence: I will tell her the news when I ___ her at the party.
gaps.hint: when clauses take present for future
gaps.explanation: Time clauses with future meaning use the present simple, not 'will': see.
